stages.name: Phoenician dynasty
stages.desc: Ruled by the Phoenician kings of Kition

stages.name: Greek dynasty
stages.desc: Local Greek-style kings; Amathus's dynasty was native Cypriot

stages.name: Persian-controlled
stages.desc: Persian forces hold the ground, or have just forced its surrender

stages.name: Under Evagoras
stages.desc: The realm of Evagoras of Salamis: his city, conquests and allies

stages.name: Ptolemaic
stages.desc: Allied to or seized by Ptolemy of Egypt

states.name: Larnaca
timeline: Kition, a Phoenician kingdom of Melqart and Astarte with a harbour for warships
King Milkyaton sets up a trophy for a victory over his enemies and their Paphian allies
Kition appeals to the Persian king against Evagoras
Evagoras holds almost the whole island; Kition is apparently overrun, though no account of its fall survives
The Persian armada gathers at Kition after defeating Evagoras offshore
The peace confines Evagoras to Salamis; Kition's dynasty recovers
Pumayyaton, son of Milkyaton, becomes king (about 362)
The revolt of the nine kings collapses and the cities submit; Kition's dynasty stays on as a Persian vassal
Persian rule ends with Alexander; Pumayyaton keeps his throne
Kition sides with Antigonus and is besieged by Seleucus for Ptolemy
Ptolemy has Pumayyaton put to death: the Phoenician dynasty of Kition ends

states.name: Famagusta
timeline: Evagoras seizes Salamis from Abdemon of Tyre
Evagoras helps prepare the fleet that defeats Sparta off Cnidus
After the defeat off Kition, Salamis is besieged by land and sea
Peace: Evagoras keeps Salamis as a king who pays tribute to Persia
Evagoras is murdered; his son Nicocles succeeds
Salamis joins the revolt of the nine kings
Besieged by a Persian-backed force under Phocion, King Pnytagoras submits (date approximate)
Pnytagoras sails to Alexander at Tyre; Persian rule ends
Nicocreon of Salamis allies with Ptolemy
Ptolemy makes Nicocreon general of Cyprus

states.name: Nicosia
timeline: Inland Idalion has been ruled from Kition since the mid-fifth century
Evagoras's conquests reach the interior
The Persian army campaigns on the island
Kition's kings rule Idalion again
The revolt collapses and the cities submit to Persia
Pumayyaton's titles now include Tamassos, the copper town (about 341)
Alexander gives Tamassos to Salamis; Kition keeps Idalion
Idalion falls to Ptolemy with Kition

states.name: Limassol
timeline: Amathus, with its native Cypriot dynasty, and Greek Kourion
Amathus appeals to the Persian king against Evagoras
Evagoras holds almost the whole island
The Persian armada controls the south coast
The peace restores the local kings
The revolt collapses and the cities submit to Persia
Androcles of Amathus sails with Alexander at Tyre
Seleucus, fighting for Ptolemy, forces Amathus to give guarantees

states.name: Paphos
timeline: The Greek kingdoms of Paphos and Marion
Paphians fight as allies of Kition's enemies, probably Evagoras
The peace strips Evagoras of his allies and conquests
The revolt collapses and the cities submit to Persia
Persian rule ends with Alexander; Nicocles reigns at Paphos by the 320s
Paphos sides with Ptolemy; Seleucus wins over Stasioecus of Marion
Ptolemy razes Marion and moves its people to Paphos

events.title: Evagoras takes Salamis
events.text: An exile returns with about fifty men, storms the palace and drives out Abdemon of Tyre.

events.title: Phoenician Kition
events.text: On the south coast, Kition is ruled by Phoenician kings who also hold inland Idalion.

events.title: The war harbour
events.text: Kition's harbour at Bamboula, in use since the fifth century, shelters triremes in ship sheds.

events.title: Conon takes refuge
events.text: After Athens loses its fleet at Aegospotami, the admiral Conon flees to Evagoras.

events.title: Ships for Conon
events.text: Persia gives Conon a naval command and orders the kings of Cyprus to prepare a hundred triremes.

events.title: Victory at Cnidus
events.text: Far to the west, Conon's Persian fleet, which Evagoras helped to raise, destroys Sparta's navy.

events.title: Honoured by Athens
events.text: Athens honours Evagoras and sets up his statue beside Conon's.

events.title: Milkyaton's trophy
events.text: Kition's king and people dedicate a trophy to Baal Oz; its first word is Greek in Phoenician letters.

events.title: Paphian allies
events.text: The trophy names the Paphians as allies of Kition's enemies, who were probably Evagoras's forces.

events.title: Envoys from Amathus
events.text: Amathus, Soloi and Kition ask Artaxerxes II for help against Evagoras.

events.title: Soloi resists
events.text: Soloi holds out against Salamis and joins the appeal to Persia.

events.title: Hecatomnus crosses
events.text: Artaxerxes orders Hecatomnus of Caria to attack, but he later funds Evagoras in secret.

events.title: Athenian squadron lost
events.text: Ten Athenian triremes bound for Evagoras are captured at sea by the Spartans.

events.title: Chabrias arrives
events.text: Athens sends Chabrias with ten ships and eight hundred light troops.

events.title: The King's Peace
events.text: Sparta and Persia's treaty assigns Cyprus to the Great King, and Athens withdraws.

events.title: Milkyaton's sixth year
events.text: A dedication shows Milkyaton still reigning over Kition and Idalion.

events.title: Almost the whole island
events.text: Diodorus records that Evagoras now holds nearly all of Cyprus.

events.title: Kition overrun
events.text: Kition apparently falls to Evagoras, though no surviving account describes it.

events.title: Tyre and Cilicia
events.text: Evagoras holds Tyre, and Cilicia rises against Persia (dates uncertain).

events.title: Egyptian alliance
events.text: Pharaoh Achoris sends ships and money to Evagoras (date uncertain).

events.title: The armada
events.text: Tiribazus and Orontes prepare a force Diodorus puts at 300 warships and 300,000 men.

events.title: Grain mutiny
events.text: A food shortage sets off a mutiny among the invaders, ended by grain from Cilicia.

events.title: Battle off Kition
events.text: Evagoras surprises the Persian fleet with 200 triremes, gains an early lead, and is beaten back.

events.title: Salamis besieged
events.text: The Persians gather at Kition, then blockade Salamis by land and sea.

events.title: Flight to Egypt
events.text: Evagoras slips away with ten triremes to seek help, returning with little.

events.title: Tiribazus arrested
events.text: Evagoras rejects terms requiring him to obey as a slave; a rival accuses Tiribazus, and he is seized.

events.title: As a king
events.text: Orontes agrees: Evagoras keeps Salamis, pays tribute and obeys as a king.

events.title: Evagoras murdered
events.text: A eunuch, named Thrasydaeus by Theopompus, kills Evagoras and his son Pnytagoras; Nicocles succeeds.

events.title: Isocrates's eulogy
events.text: The Athenian orator praises Evagoras in a prose eulogy addressed to Nicocles (date approximate).

events.title: Pumayyaton crowned
events.text: Milkyaton's son begins a fifty-year reign over Kition and Idalion (about 362).

events.title: Nine kings revolt
events.text: Following the Phoenician cities, the nine kings of Cyprus declare independence from Persia.

events.title: Phocion at Salamis
events.text: Forty triremes and 8,000 mercenaries from Caria besiege Salamis; its king submits (date approximate).

events.title: The cities surrender
events.text: While Salamis is under siege, every other Cypriot city submits to Persia.

events.title: King of Tamassos
events.text: An altar of about 341 gives Pumayyaton the title king of Kition, Idalion and Tamassos.

events.title: Zeno is born
events.text: Zeno, the future founder of Stoicism, is born at Kition (about 334).

events.title: Kitians in Athens
events.text: Athens lets Kitian merchants acquire land for a temple of their Aphrodite.

events.title: The fleet at Tyre
events.text: The kings of Cyprus bring about 120 ships to Alexander's siege of Tyre.

events.title: Tamassos lost
events.text: Alexander takes Tamassos from Pumayyaton and gives it to Salamis.

events.title: The island divides
events.text: Salamis and other kingdoms back Ptolemy; Kition, Lapithos, Marion and Keryneia back Antigonus.

events.title: North coast taken
events.text: Seleucus, fighting for Ptolemy, captures Keryneia and Lapithos.

events.title: Kition besieged
events.text: Kition refuses to join Seleucus, who besieges it with all his forces.

events.title: Pumayyaton executed
events.text: Ptolemy has Kition's king put to death for dealing with Antigonus, ending the dynasty.

events.title: Marion razed
events.text: Ptolemy destroys Marion and moves its people to Paphos.

events.title: King of Lapithos arrested
events.text: Ptolemy seizes Praxippus, king of Lapithos.

events.title: Nicocreon made general
events.text: Nicocreon of Salamis takes command of Cyprus for Ptolemy; the last kings fall by about 310.

chartNote: Share of the area of five modern districts, used as stand-ins for the ancient kingdoms. This is a simplification: boundaries are today's, the kingdoms did not match them, and Famagusta, standing for Salamis, is small because only the district's southern part is drawn. The north of the island, including the site of Salamis itself, is not coloured. Many dates are approximate, and Kition's fall to Evagoras is inferred.
